title: Contract-enforcer middleware for telemetry ingestion
creator: Anika Rao
description: Implement a lightweight, runtime 'contract-enforcer' middleware positioned in the telemetry ingestion path that validates incoming usage events against a versioned schema registry, emits rich rejection diagnostics, and routes malformed or incompatible payloads to a dead-letter queue for offline analysis. The goal is to reduce downstream schema churn in analytics pipelines, improve pipeline SLOs by failing fast on invalid events, and provide clear actionable feedback to SDK/agent teams.
acceptance_criteria: All inbound telemetry events are validated against the active schema version before being enqueued to the streaming topic
Schema mismatches result in a structured rejection event emitted to the DLQ with reason, field path, and example payload
Validation latency added by middleware stays < 3ms p50 under normal load and < 8ms p95 under 99th percentile traffic
Automated canary rollout for contract changes: 1% traffic can opt-in to new schema version before full promotion
Integration tests cover core schema rules (required fields, field types, enum constraints), and e2e tests validate DLQ routing
comments: 2026-02-05 - Anika Rao: Initial ticket drafted after several incidents where downstream analytics jobs failed due to unexpected event shapes. Proposal: middleware validates JSON events using JSON Schema v2019-09 stored in a versioned registry (S3 + Dynamo index).

2026-02-12 - Jared Kim: Spike complete. Built a Go prototype validating events with gojsonschema; measured median validation cost ~1.2ms for typical event (~1.1KB). Identified GC pressure under high concurrency; exploring reuse of compiled schemas and object pooling.

2026-02-18 - Infra review (Lina Park): Prefer schema compile-once approach and keep compiled artifacts in-memory behind LRU keyed by schema-version. Suggest using Kafka topic partitions + backpressure instead of sync writes to S3 for registry reads during bootstrapping.

2026-02-23 - Decision: Use compiled JSON Schema with a lightweight in-process cache; registry stored in S3 with a Dynamo manifest. New schema promotion will write a manifest record that ingestion instances poll every 30s. For faster rollout we will support a push endpoint via Control Plane (separate PR).
2026-03-02 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1842 — includes middleware, unit tests, and a fake DLQ writer for local dev. Seeking review from Observability and SDK teams.

2026-03-05 - Review notes (Observability): Add rejection counters broken down by schema_version and rule_type (missing_field, type_mismatch, enum_failed). Also request tracing integration to attach trace_id from header when present.

2026-03-07 - Performance testing: Ran a 10m soak at production-like QPS (7k rps). p50 latency added by middleware 1.6ms, p95 6.9ms. Heap growth stabilized after introducing object pooling and reuse of validator instances.

2026-03-10 - Rollout plan discussed with SRE: Start with internal-only topic and 1% production traffic canary for 24h. If no regressions, increase to 25% then 100% over 48h windows. Failure modes annotated in runbook (reject storms, registry unreachability).

2026-03-12 - QA: Added e2e test that injects malformed events and asserts DLQ entries and dashboard counters. Added test for canary opt-in header 'X-Schema-Canary' to exercise dual-version validation path.
